memory_verse.label: Bible Reference

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Days ago Pharaoh stood in the dark, surrounded by grief, begging Moses to leave
and even asking for a blessing. Now he says, "What have we done?"

This is what worldly sorrow looks like when the pressure lifts. Paul described
it exactly: godly sorrow leads to repentance, but worldly sorrow only regrets
the cost (2 Cor 7:10). Pharaoh had not changed. He had merely been squeezed, and
now that the squeezing had stopped, the old man was back.

Look at what he actually mourns: "We have lost their services." Not the death of
his son. Not the ruin of his country. His labour force.

That is the honest heart of hardness. Even after catastrophe, what he valued was
what he could extract from people.

There is a warning here for all of us. It is possible to be deeply moved by a
crisis, to make promises to God in a hospital corridor or a difficult season,
and then to quietly return to who we were once life becomes comfortable again.
The test of repentance is not the intensity of the moment. It is what we are
still doing six months later.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What did you promise God in a hard season that you have quietly dropped?
2. Are there people in your life you mainly value for what they do for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep my repentance real. Do not let me return to what You brought me out
of once the pressure eases. Amen.
